title: Palestinian Killed in Settler Raid on Hajja Village; Second Palestinian Shot Dead After Stabbing Israeli Near Qusra
detail: Violence flared across the northern West Bank on Monday, September 7, 2026. Overnight, roughly nine armed settlers from a nearby outpost raided Hajja village; when more than 100 residents rushed to confront them, Israeli troops approached from the opposite direction, trapping Palestinians between the soldiers and the settlers. The military said Palestinians threw stones and troops responded with warning shots and live fire; both settlers and soldiers opened fire. The Palestinian Health Ministry said Omar al-Tubasi, 20 (reported elsewhere as 19), died of a gunshot wound to the head, and three others were wounded. In a separate incident near Qusra village -- site of a settler siege that drew international outcry in August -- a Palestinian entered a settler outpost and stabbed a 20-year-old Israeli, critically wounding him, then tried to stab soldiers; a military commander shot and killed the 34-year-old assailant. Prime Minister Netanyahu said Israel would 'continue to eliminate terrorists,' referencing recent US pressure over settler violence, and defended his government's support for outposts that lack formal approval but are frequently granted retroactive legal status.

confidenceReason: Reported by Reuters with named correspondents and corroborated by Al-Monitor and Palestinian Information Center reporting, including named victims (Omar al-Tubasi) from the Palestinian Health Ministry; IDF account of the sequence of events differs on responsibility but does not dispute the deaths occurred.

title: ICJ Opens Hearings on Germany's Bid to Dismiss Nicaragua's Gaza Genocide-Complicity Case
detail: The International Court of Justice opened four days of public hearings (September 7-10, 2026) on preliminary objections raised by Germany in the case 'Alleged Breaches of Certain International Obligations in respect of the Occupied Palestinian Territory' (Nicaragua v. Germany), filed by Nicaragua in March 2024. Nicaragua argues Germany violated the 1948 Genocide Convention and the Geneva Conventions by continuing to supply Israel with military equipment and by defunding UNRWA despite an asserted recognized risk of genocide in Gaza since October 2023. Germany contends the ICJ lacks jurisdiction and that Nicaragua failed to satisfy required procedural preconditions, and says 98% of its post-October 7, 2023 military exports to Israel were non-lethal (helmets, binoculars, etc.). Judges are expected to rule on jurisdiction within roughly six months; if the case proceeds to merits, it would run in parallel with South Africa's genocide case against Israel (ICJ Case 192), whose own discovery schedule extends to 2029.
